summary.title: We Hire the Best, Just Like Everyone Else
summary.one_liner: Jeff Atwood argues that the "only hire the best" startup advice is flawed, citing bias and the "People Like Us" problem, and suggests audition projects and broader hiring as alternatives.
takeaways: Strict 'only hire the best' policies can accidentally optimize for implicit bias and exclude good candidates.
Bad hires are costly and hard to fire, but rejecting good candidates has its own costs, so the trade-off needs judgment.
Paid audition projects (contract work of several weeks) let companies and candidates evaluate fit with real tasks.
Expanding the hiring pool geographically and beyond 'People Like Us' networks can improve diversity and talent access.
summary.summary: This Coding Horror blog post by Jeff Atwood challenges the common startup advice to hire only the best. He quotes Guy Kawasaki, Jon Soberg, and Joel Spolsky on the risks of mediocre hires and the rigor they recommend, then argues that such strictness leads to bias and reduces diversity, citing the People Like Us problem and studies on hidden bias. He closes by recommending broader geographic sourcing and paid audition projects, as used by Automattic, where candidates do real work for three to eight weeks before a hiring decision.
